prompt: Use case: concept design sheet for a rideable bicycle in the game Yorimichi, a painterly Japanese island game. Image 1 is an in-game screenshot showing the player character Cairo, a 148 cm boy with spiky black hair, a loose yellow T-shirt over white long sleeves, olive cargo trousers and white sneakers, and the game's soft, clean, lightly stylized 3D look. Image 2 is an approved art-direction painting from the same game: warm beige concrete, deep indigo steel, wave and sunburst murals, maple leaves, teal and ochre accents. Paint a clean design sheet on warm off-white paper with four candidate bicycles, each in a pure side elevation facing right, in a 2x2 grid with generous spacing, all at the same scale and sized for a 148 cm child (24-inch wheels). Each bike must be mechanically correct and buildable as a game asset: exactly two wheels with visible spokes, one chainring on the right side, one chain loop to the rear sprocket, two pedal cranks pointing in opposite directions, a saddle on a seat post, handlebars joined to the fork through the head tube. A: a Japanese mamachari step-through city bike, deep teal frame, cream fenders, a woven wicker front basket, a rear rack, a chrome bell, a round front lamp, a full chain guard with a cream sunburst motif, a two-leg kickstand. B: a sturdy 24-inch BMX-style street bike, deep indigo frame, gum-wall tyres, an ochre number plate with a small wave emblem, axle pegs, a padded crossbar. C: a small vintage randonneur with upright swept-back bars, an ochre frame, cream mudguards, a tan leather saddle, a canvas front bag and a maple-leaf head badge. D: a compact mini-velo with 20-inch wheels and a flat wooden front cargo tray, a vermilion frame and cream tyres. Soft flat painterly shading matching image 2, crisp readable silhouettes, no people, no scenery, a small hand-lettered capital A, B, C or D under each bike and no other text.

Keep the sword and skateboard only in their insets and on the three-quarter view. No people, no text, no labels, no arrows.
